Noun

sega (Balinese script ᬲᭂᬕ)

  1. cooked rice

Italian

[edit]
Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
sega
Wikipedia it

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈse.ɡa/
  • Rhymes: -eɡa
  • Hyphenation: sé‧ga

Etymology 1

[edit]

From the verb segare. Related to French scie, as well as (through Indo-European) German Säge, English saw, and other Germanic cognates.

Noun

[edit]

sega f (plural seghe)

  1. saw
  2. (vulgar) wank, handjob
    farsi una sega
    to jerk off, to wank
  3. (vulgar, chiefly in the negative) worth shit
    Synonyms: un cazzo (literally “a dick's worth”), da quattro soldi (literally “four coins' worth”), una lira, un centesimo
    quest'auto non vale una sega
    this car isn't worth shit
Related terms
[edit]
  • motosega
  • sega a dorso
  • sega a nastro
  • sega ad arco
  • sega circolare
  • sega mentale
  • segaiolo
  • segare
  • segarsi
  • segatronchi
  • segheria

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

sega

  1. inflection of segare:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Latvian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From segt (“to cover”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sæɡa]
This entry needs an audio pronunciation. If you are a native speaker with a microphone, please record this word. The recorded pronunciation will appear here when it's ready.

Noun

[edit]

sega f (4th declension)

  1. blanket, quilt (large cloth used for covering, especially a bedcover)
    gultas sega ― bed blanket, cover
    bieza, silta sega ― thick, warm blanket
    ietīties, ievīstīties segā ― to wrap oneself in a blanket
    vatēta sega ― quilt blanket, comforter
    dekoratīva sienas sega ― decorative wall quilt
    kamanu sega ― sleigh blanket, cover
    galvas sega, galvassega ― headcovering (hats, scarves, etc.)
    ceļa sega ― road pavement
  2. a layer (of something) that covers (something else)
    bieza sniega sega ― a thick snow layer
    seglu, galda sega ― saddle, table cover
    asfalta sega ― a layer of asphalt (e.g., on a road)
    augu sega ― a layer of plants, vegetation
  3. clouds, fog, smoke, vapors (seen as covering something)
    zila dūmu sega ― a blanket of blue smoke
    tumšpelēkā mākoņu sega virs māju jumtiem ― a dark gray blanket of clouds over house roofs

Swedish

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Japanese セガ (Sega).

Noun

[edit]

sega n

  1. alternative letter-case form of Sega
Declension
[edit]
Declension of sega
nominative genitive
singular indefinite sega segas
definite segat segats
plural indefinite — —
definite — —

Etymology 2

[edit]

seg +‎ -a

Verb

[edit]

sega (present segar, preterite segade, supine segat, imperative sega)

  1. (often reflexive) to move slowly
    Kön segar sig fram
    The queue slowly moves forward
  2. (colloquial, often reflexive) to be tardy (slow)
    De skulle kommit för en timme sen. Måste de sega hela tiden?
    They were supposed to be here an hour ago. Do they have to be so slow all the time?
    Sluta sega dig
    Hurry up
